local_checks.invariant: Per-IP rate limiting on public routes must key on an address the client cannot choose; trustProxy must trust only the known edge hop.
local_checks.result: buildApp sets trustProxy: true, so request.ip is the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry. In the sandboxed test with the production default waitlist limiter (5 per 10 min), one socket peer sending a fixed real-client XFF got 202x5 then 429. The same peer rotating a client-supplied leftmost XFF entry ('203.0.113.N, 198.51.100.9') got 202 on all 20 attempts, and request.ip came back as the spoofed 203.0.113.77. Whether this can be exploited in production depends on whether Railway's edge appends to or overwrites an incoming X-Forwarded-For header, and source does not show that.

local_checks.invariant: GET /waitlist/stats requires a strong admin bearer token compared in constant time, and is hidden when unset.
local_checks.result: Returns 404 when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset. The config rejects tokens under 32 characters. tokenMatches compares SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual. The route returns only aggregate counts, no emails. No default or hard-coded admin token exists.

local_checks.invariant: No open redirect, reflected markup or enumeration on the waitlist and landing routes.
local_checks.result: The waitlist form redirect target is fixed to /join or /he/join. Source is regex-limited to [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} and URLSearchParams-encoded. GET / redirects to the fixed /join or /he/join plus the original query string, so no host or path is under attacker control. renderLandingPage HTML-escapes every placeholder and validates source. A strict CSP is set (no inline script, frame-ancestors 'none'). POST /waitlist answers the same way for new and existing emails. Unsubscribe uses 192-bit random tokens of at most 128 characters and shows the same page for unknown tokens.

local_checks.invariant: Unauthenticated health, app-link and static routes expose no secrets, debug state or filesystem paths.

local_checks.invariant: No committed secrets, no prod-usable defaults, debug not toggleable, safe container and error behaviour.
local_checks.result: Both .gitignore files cover .env. .env.example has every secret blank (DATABASE_URL is a localhost dev default only). local_checks.invariant: Apple identity tokens are accepted only with a signature from Apple's JWKS, a pinned RS256 algorithm, issuer https://appleid.apple.com, an audience in APPLE_AUDIENCES, a non-empty sub, and nonce == sha256(raw nonce); the user is keyed only by the verified sub
local_checks.result: jose jwtVerify gets the remote JWKS (kid selects only within Apple's set, no jku/x5u), algorithms ['RS256'], issuer and audience pinned, exp/nbf checked by jose by default. sub type and nonce are checked after verification. All other errors become InvalidAppleTokenError and a 401. The upsert keys on identity.sub only, and the client name cannot change identity. No decode-without-verify path.

local_checks.invariant: Session JWTs verify with an HS256-only, server-held secret of at least 32 characters and a pinned issuer and audience; a missing or invalid bearer gives a 401
local_checks.result: JwtService.verify pins algorithms ['HS256'], issuer 'dog-monitor', audience 'dog-monitor-app'. jose enforces exp. requireServerConfig rejects a missing JWT_SECRET or one under 32 chars. The plugin accepts only 'Bearer ' and returns 401 when claims are null. Apple tokens (RS256, a different iss and aud) cannot pass. No alg-none or key-confusion path.

x_hardening: Session JWTs (30-day default) have no revocation or jti. Removing a member is enforced by requireHousehold's membership lookup, not by token invalidation, so a leaked session stays valid for /me and household creation until exp.

The Apple sign-in nonce is generated by the client and not recorded as used on the server. A captured (identityToken, rawNonce) pair can be replayed within the Apple token's lifetime. Getting the pair requires the TLS request body, so this is not a finding.

local_checks.result: Holds. alg is pinned to ES256 in both the header check and compactVerify. local_checks.invariant: The session JWT and the device secret are stored only in a Keychain item that other apps, backups or other devices cannot read.
local_checks.result: Both credentials go to a kSecClassGenericPassword item (service com.benooon.dogmonitor, account dogmonitor.credential) with kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, so the item is excluded from backups and device migration. No kSecAttrAccessGroup is set. project.yml declares only application-groups and no keychain-access-groups, so the item stays in the app's default access group. InMemorySecureStore appears only in previews and tests. Swift is source-only (no toolchain); the final entitlements match the source declarations.

local_checks.result: Grep found UserDefaults and App Group usage only for non-secret state: role, zones, the push device id, and dog status snapshots/photos in group.com.benooon.dogmonitor. Logger calls never interpolate the token, the secret or the Authorization header. signOut clears the Keychain item.

local_checks.invariant: The Authorization credential is sent only to the configured HTTPS API origin, and never to presigned storage URLs.
local_checks.result: makeRequest and realtimeRequest attach Authorization only to baseURL-derived URLs. The presigned-PUT upload sends no credential. The http://localhost:3000 fallback applies only when the Info.plist key is missing, and the realtime socket uses wss when the base URL is https.

local_checks.invariant: Credentials placed on the general pasteboard are bounded in lifetime and readable only with user consent.
local_checks.result: The owner's 'Copy export key' button places the 1-hour training export JWT on UIPasteboard.general without an expirationDate or localOnly option. On iOS 17+ another app needs the system paste-consent prompt to read it, and Universal Clipboard reaches only the same Apple ID. The user copies it on purpose to paste on a computer. Not a boundary violation (recorded as hardening). The token's full session power is a separate issue owned by the training export-token unit.

x_hardening: backend/src/routes/landing.ts:89 publicOrigin uses request.host, which trustProxy: true takes from X-Forwarded-Host. The value is regex-limited to hostname characters, HTML-escaped, and the page is served with cache-control: no-cache, so it only spoofs OG/canonical URLs in the attacker's own response. A configured PUBLIC_ORIGIN would remove this.

ios/App/Household/HouseholdView.swift:201 copies the 1-hour export JWT to UIPasteboard.general without an expiry. setItems with an .expirationDate matching the token TTL would limit how long it stays on the clipboard and in Universal Clipboard.
